lead: >-
  Colombia's beach tours differ in how long you can relax beside the Caribbean Sea. On Barú, you can enjoy several free days after Bogotá and Cartagena; on San Andrés, stay at an island hotel; and in the Rosario Islands, take a day trip or stay for several nights. On other itineraries, the coast is just one part of a sightseeing journey. Choose by the actual number of free days by the water, domestic flights, boat transfers and the conditions of the specific tour.
---

## How to choose a beach tour in Colombia

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a beach component in Colombia. Options range from short trips to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) with one day on the islands to extensive journeys through the Andes and coffee region, as well as itineraries with several nights on the coast. **Compare the actual days of each itinerary, not merely its label as a “beach tour”.** Sometimes that means a proper hotel-based seaside holiday; sometimes it means a boat excursion between city tours.

| Where to relax | What the programme offers |
|---|---|
| [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/) | Several nights by the sea |
| [San Andrés](/colombia/place/san-andres/) | An island resort stay |
| [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) | A day trip or overnight stays |
| [Tayrona](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) | A nature excursion |

Barú can be reached from Cartagena by road or boat. The Rosario Islands are an archipelago reached by speedboat. San Andrés lies far offshore and requires a separate flight. Tayrona involves walking trails, national park regulations and beaches where swimming is permitted. Even within the Caribbean region, the travel arrangements therefore differ considerably.

## Barú: free beach days after cities and coffee country

On the [10-day “Colombia VIP: Bogotá, Coffee Region, Cartagena and Barú” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/), the seaside portion comes towards the end. First are Bogotá, [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), the coffee region and Cartagena sightseeing. Day seven includes a boat trip to Barú and check-in at Las Islas, in a bungalow with a private pool. **Days eight and nine are free of a packed sightseeing schedule.** Day ten is for returning to Cartagena and departing.

The same itinerary names Four Seasons Casa Medina in Bogotá and Sofitel Legend Santa Clara in Cartagena. These are details of that particular option, not promises that every beach tour uses the same hotels. International and domestic flights are listed among the services paid for separately.

The [12-day Colombia group tour with a stay on Barú](/colombia/tour/colombia-baru-beach-group-tour-12-days/) visits Bogotá, [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and Cartagena. Arrival on Barú is scheduled for day eight, days nine and ten are for relaxation, day eleven for returning to Cartagena and day twelve for departure. Once again, count the genuinely free days at the beach separately from arrival and the return journey.

**Choose between these itineraries based on travel format, sightseeing stops, accommodation and included services.** The first has an extensive coffee-country section and specifies private transfers; the second is a group journey including Medellín. Their time by the sea is comparable, but prices and conditions are specific to each tour. A beach stop does not automatically include scuba diving, private boat hire or all-inclusive meals.

Barú is often called an island, although geographically it is a peninsula. It has different beach areas and facilities, including Playa Blanca and Agua Azul. If you want to see it without spending several nights on the coast, there is a separate [Barú excursion with a beach day at Agua Azul](/colombia/baru-island/colombia-baru-agua-azul-day-trip/). Its inclusions must be assessed separately from the multi-day itineraries.

## San Andrés: a resort island requiring a separate flight

The [12-day Colombia tour with beach time](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-beaches-12-days/) combines Bogotá, [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/), the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and Cartagena. A flight to San Andrés and accommodation at Decameron Isleño ALL IN are planned for day five. **Days six to eight are set aside for island relaxation**, after which the trip continues via Medellín, Guatapé and Bogotá. This option provides three full island days after sightseeing.

The [11-day “Colombia in All Its Diversity” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) also passes through the coffee region, Cartagena and San Andrés, but in a different order. The island flight falls on day six, days seven and eight are for relaxing, and the flight to Medellín is scheduled for day nine. That means **two full days beside the Caribbean Sea**. Comparing overall durations of 11 and 12 days without examining their routes would be misleading.

[San Andrés](/colombia/place/san-andres/) lies a long way from mainland Colombia. The archipelago is known for coral reefs, differently coloured waters and its distinctive island culture. On the island itself, there are town beaches by hotels and a promenade, as well as more remote coastal stretches. A hotel's location and planned activities matter at least as much as its room category.

For these tours, check the inclusion of domestic air tickets, meals and transfers particularly carefully. The words ALL IN in one hotel's name do not apply to every Ada Tours itinerary. Special tourist formalities also apply on San Andrés, including a tourist card; the current procedure and charge should be checked against the rules in force before travelling. An extra island day offers more swimming time, but increases the length of accommodation and flight-logistics requirements.

## Rosario Islands: an overnight stay or a single boat excursion

The [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) lie off Cartagena. This is a separate archipelago with beaches, coral reefs and protected marine areas. A day trip there and back gives visitors a chance to see the islands and spend several hours by the water. Staying overnight changes the experience: you gain quiet mornings and evenings without having to return to the city every day.

We offer both options:

- The [14-day “Colombia” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-2024/) combines Bogotá, the coffee region, Medellín and Cartagena with several days in the Rosario Islands. Travellers arrive on the islands on day nine; days ten to twelve are spent there, with day thirteen reserved for the return journey through Cartagena.
- The [5-day “From the Andes to the Caribbean Sea” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/) includes a day-four trip to San Pedro de Majagua in the Rosario Islands, returning to Cartagena for the night.
- The [7-day “Colombia Highlights”](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) and [9-day “Colombia in Four Chapters”](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) also feature a single day at San Pedro de Majagua, on days six and eight respectively.
- The [8-day Bogotá–Medellín–Cartagena tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-cultural-tour-8-days/) visits the Rosario Islands on day seven. The [6-day Bogotá and Cartagena tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-culture-6-days-2024/) does so on day five.

You can also consider a separate [Rosario Islands excursion from Cartagena](/colombia/rosario-islands/rosario-islands-tour-from-cartagena/) or [a day at San Pedro de Majagua](/colombia/rosario-islands/colombia-san-pedro-de-majagua-day-trip/). Each has its own description and terms. For instance, the five-day itinerary specifies a shared speedboat, Caribbean lunch, dessert, coffee or tea and a marine fee for the San Pedro de Majagua trip. A private boat is available for an additional charge. **These inclusions belong to that particular programme**, not automatically to every archipelago excursion.

Sea conditions can affect the boat crossing and whether departures operate. On a trip lasting only a few days, leave sufficient time before an evening flight: returning from the islands and connecting to the airport is not equivalent to several free hours on the beach. For travellers seeking unhurried relaxation, the number of nights in the archipelago matters more than simply seeing Rosario Islands in a tour title.

## Santa Marta and Tayrona: when the coast is part of a nature itinerary

Not all our beach-themed tours are designed for leisurely stays at a coastal hotel. On the [13-day “Colombia Live” itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-live/), [Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/) and [Tayrona](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) follow Bogotá and coffee country, with Cartagena afterward. Day nine focuses on the park and Cabo San Juan; other days feature history, nature and food experiences. The beach is one element of a larger journey.

On the [10-day “Wonders of Colombia” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-villa-de-leyva/), Tayrona National Park features on day seven after Bogotá, Villa de Leyva and coffee-growing areas. Meanwhile, the [7-day Lost City route](/colombia/tour/santa-marta-lost-city-2023/) is primarily a trek from the Santa Marta area, followed by a visit to the national park. Choose that journey for the hiking and extended walking involved, not as a substitute for a resort holiday.

The [15-day itinerary through Bogotá, Medellín, Santa Marta and Rosario Islands](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-cartagena-medellin-rosario-islands-santa-marta/) also includes a multi-day Lost City trek, with a boat excursion towards the end. It is a busy trip with one island day, not an uninterrupted seaside holiday.

[Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) demands different preparation from staying in a beach hotel. Swimming is permitted only in designated areas, and some beaches are closed because of dangerous waves and currents. The park periodically suspends visitor access for ecological recovery and cultural practices of local communities; additional safety restrictions are possible. Check entrances, trail availability and swimming rules for your specific dates. A separate [excursion from Santa Marta to Tayrona and Playa Cristal](/colombia/santa-marta/tayrona-national-park-playa-cristal/) has its own conditions.

## Combining the Caribbean Sea with the Andes and coffee region

You can put the beach stay at the end of the trip after busy city and nature days. But flights between [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) take up part of the itinerary. Arrival day at the coast cannot be counted as a full free day: it often includes an airport transfer, a flight, the journey to the hotel and check-in.

For a short trip, choose Bogotá, Cartagena and one boat excursion. Adding Medellín expands a seven-day journey, but Rosario Islands still accounts for only one day. A nine-day option adds coffee country and active pursuits while keeping the same principle of a separate island outing.

If [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/), the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and coffee farms interest you, compare [Colombia's coffee tours](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/colombia/) as well. For more in-depth visits to historic cities and museums, see [Colombia's cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/). These collections help you choose the substantive part of the journey but do not themselves add nights on the beach.

If the main objective is the sea, first decide which region suits you and how many nights you want by the water. Add cities only afterward: extra transfers can consume valuable free hours.

## Seasons and conditions for boat journeys

Colombia's Caribbean coast is warm for much of the year, but rain, wind and sea conditions vary by place and month. For San Andrés, the national tourism authority identifies a comparatively dry period from roughly December to May and a wetter one from June to November. These are seasonal guidelines, not a guarantee for a particular week.

Sea conditions around Barú and Rosario affect boat services. Even under clear skies, a crossing may need to be rescheduled. At Tayrona, national park rules and seasonal closures add to the weather constraints. Choose dates based on the final beach destination rather than the average temperature for Colombia as a whole.

Before booking, establish the following:

1. **How many full days by the sea** remain after deducting transfers, excursions and your departure flight.
2. **Where the hotel is:** in Cartagena, on Barú, in the Rosario Islands or on San Andrés. These options offer very different amounts of time by the water.
3. **What your exact tour includes:** domestic air tickets, boats, marine fees, transfers, meals, guides and excursions.
4. **Which restrictions apply** to island boat trips and entry to Tayrona on your intended dates.
5. **Which activities are optional:** diving, private boat hire, additional outings and other services beyond the basic itinerary.

Inclusions vary from one tour to another. One programme confirms lunch in Rosario; another names specific hotels on Barú; a third excludes some flights. Compare the exact tour description with your plans for free days.

## Frequently asked questions about Colombia beach tours

### Where is best for two or three free days by the sea?

For that purpose, compare [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/), [San Andrés](/colombia/place/san-andres/) and a multi-day stay in the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/). Some tours have two or three full free days. A day trip to the islands serves a different purpose: experiencing the archipelago without an overnight stay.

### Are Barú and the Rosario Islands the same place?

No. Geographically Barú is a peninsula near Cartagena, although it is often called an island. The Rosario Islands form a separate archipelago. Some trips include a boat and seaside accommodation; others involve only a boat excursion returning in the evening. Check the day-by-day itinerary for overnight stays.

### Can I combine the sea with coffee plantations?

Yes. The [10-day VIP route with Barú](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/), the [12-day programme with San Andrés](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-beaches-12-days/) and the [11-day “Colombia in All Its Diversity”](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) combine coffee-growing regions with the coast. They differ in the number of beach days, journey sequence and excursion activities.

### Do I need a separate flight to San Andrés?

Yes. On the named programmes, the flight to San Andrés is a separate itinerary leg. It takes up part of a day, and its inclusion in the tour price depends on the specific programme. A boat is used for a Rosario Islands excursion from Cartagena; no separate flight is needed.

### Can I swim at any beach in Tayrona?

No. Swimming is allowed only in designated places; some beaches have dangerous waves and currents. Temporary park closures are also possible. Check current rules and dates before travelling, even if a Tayrona visit appears in your tour description.

### How should I choose a programme if I mainly want a beach holiday?

Choose by accommodation location and the number of free days by the sea, then compare flights and inclusions. If you only want a single day at sea, consider a [Rosario Islands excursion from Cartagena](/colombia/rosario-islands/rosario-islands-tour-from-cartagena/). For several quieter days in one location, look at itineraries with overnight stays on Barú, in Rosario or on San Andrés.

lead: >-
  A beach holiday in Costa Rica can be combined with volcanoes, cloud forests and wildlife watching. Ada Tours' ready-made itineraries range from shorter trips with two free days beside the ocean and journeys with extended beach stays to a major private tour ending at Playa Conchal. Compare the number of genuinely free days, chosen coast, transfers and season rather than just the total trip duration.
---

## Costa Rica beach tours: start by counting the days at the sea

**If the ocean is your main reason to travel, choose the route according to how many days you will actually spend on the coast.** Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include beach time in Costa Rica. On some itineraries, the coast is the main part of the holiday; on others, it is the finale of an extensive journey through nature. Some offers also cross several Central American countries.

Distinguish three different kinds of day: a transfer to the coast, a visit to a seaside national park, and a free beach day. Each can be enjoyable, but the experience is different. If a long drive leaves only an evening by the water, that should not count as a full day at the beach.

Most beach stops on our itineraries are on the **Pacific coast**, including [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/), [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/), the [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) area and the country's wider [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/). Swimming, surfing and transport conditions vary. Choose a particular beach after examining the route instead of substituting one resort for every mention of the ocean.

## How ready-made itineraries differ in their beach component

| Tour | What the traveller gets |
|---|---|
| [“Short but Complete Programme”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/) | 7 days; Tamarindo and 2 free days |
| [“Beach and Mountains Holiday”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-beaches-mountains/) | 9 days; mountains followed by coast |
| [“3 Perspectives on Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/) | 10 days; city, volcanoes and ocean |
| [16-day premium tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) | Nature regions and Playa Conchal |
| [Guatemala and Costa Rica](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-costa-rica/) | 15 days; two countries and beach at the end |

This comparison reflects the published routes, not an identical package of services. Hotels, excursions and included meals vary. The catalogue also contains nature and adventure journeys where the beach is an additional programme element. Choose those primarily for the overall itinerary.

### Seven days: volcanoes and two free days in Tamarindo

The [7-day “Short but Complete Programme” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/) begins in central Costa Rica, taking in volcanic areas, [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/) and nature stops. On day four, the route reaches [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/), leaving days five and six free. Day seven is for the return journey.

This suits travellers with about a week who want to explore tropical nature and finish by the Pacific Ocean. The two free days can be spent on the beach or on independently selected activities. Excursions merely listed as possible extras do not automatically become included services.

**The limitation of this short route is its busy first half.** Transfers between nature regions mean it cannot be treated as a full week at a beach resort. On the other hand, two distinct free days by the ocean make the holiday structure clear from the outset.

### Nine days: Rincón de la Vieja, Monteverde and the ocean

The [9-day “Beach and Mountains Holiday” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-beaches-mountains/) starts in Liberia and crosses [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/), the [Tenorio](/costa-rica/place/tenorio-volcano-national-park/) area, [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). Day seven includes a transfer to the northern Pacific coast, day eight is devoted to relaxation and day nine to departure.

The programme is substantially more active than its “beach holiday” title might suggest. Canopy activities, river adventures, walks and hot springs may be available. It is designed for travellers who want to **explore mountains and forests first** and leave the sea until the end.

If you want four or five completely free days on the coast, compare the ten-day programmes below. The nine-day route's strength is the diversity of natural experiences.

### Ten days: two ways to combine Arenal with the Pacific

The [“3 Perspectives on Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/) has a similar geographical sequence: the capital, a coffee plantation, volcanoes, waterfalls and the ocean. This programme also offers several consecutive free days on the coast. When comparing the options, examine each day's description, accommodation, terms and included services: similar places on the map do not necessarily make two offers identical.

Both routes especially appeal to travellers who want **a genuinely extended break beside the ocean after sightseeing**. They offer more opportunity to stay in one coastal area than a journey that crosses the entire country and changes hotels frequently.

### Sixteen days: nature regions and the Playa Conchal resort

The [16-day private premium tour of Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) covers significantly more territory. The itinerary features [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), Arenal, [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/), the [Osa Peninsula](/costa-rica/place/osa-peninsula/), [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) and a boat excursion to [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/).

The journey ends with several days at [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/). The final portion of this tour includes **The Westin Playa Conchal Resort & Spa** with all-inclusive accommodation and meals. That arrangement belongs to this specific itinerary, not every Ada Tours beach programme. Different hotels and meal plans are used on individual nature sections.

Choose this route if you want the beach **after an extensive journey through parks and forests**, rather than instead of one. It involves far more nature-region transfers, boat sections and active days than the ten-day option reaching the coast earlier.

### Fifteen days: the beach after Guatemala

The [15-day “Guatemala and Costa Rica” journey](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-costa-rica/) connects colonial [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) and Costa Rica's nature regions. The latter part includes [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) and the Pacific coast, with free beach days.

This demonstrates why a trip's total duration can be misleading. Those 15 days are shared between two countries, historic towns, parks, a flight and the sea. If you mainly want the beach, a shorter trip within Costa Rica alone may offer more free time on the coast.

Other combinations appear in our [multi-country journeys catalogue](/multi-country/). For each, verify whether the beach is part of the main programme and which country it is in: a thematic label does not itself promise a lengthy resort holiday specifically in Costa Rica.

## Choosing a section of the Pacific coast

### Tamarindo and Guanacaste: more opportunities to stay by the sea

[Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/) is an accessible choice for a beach stop on itineraries through northwestern Costa Rica. You can enjoy free days by the water, stroll through the seaside town and, if you wish, try surfing. Waves and currents differ between beaches; choose a swimming spot based on the particular section and current warnings.

[Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/) is another Guanacaste option, known for shell sand and resort accommodation on one of our itineraries. Independent beach days and all-inclusive arrangements are specifically described in the [16-day private tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/); do not assume they apply to other journeys simply because they visit the region.

[Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/) and the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/) offer another reason to explore the northern coast: boat outings and underwater activities. But visiting the islands, scuba diving and several hotel-based beach days are distinct products. On the [“Extreme Costa Rica” adventure tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), marine activities complement an active programme; compare that journey by exertion as well as ocean access.

### Manuel Antonio: forest and beach in one day

[Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) is on the central Pacific coast. Around the national park, forest trails meet sandy beaches, making it possible to combine a protected-area walk with time by the water. Nearby [Quepos](/costa-rica/place/quepos/) features on itineraries through this region.

However, **an excursion to a national park is not the same as a free day at a resort**. Protected-area rules govern the visit, and beach time depends on the day selected, access hours and the actual tour schedule. If you want to spend every day beside the sea without required excursions, look at the length of the subsequent beach stay.

### The Caribbean coast: a different calendar and different journeys

[Puerto Viejo](/costa-rica/place/puerto-viejo/) and the surrounding Caribbean coast offer a different atmosphere: tropical beaches, small settlements, humid forest and their own weather patterns. This region is worth considering when planning independently, especially for dates when heavy rain falls on the Pacific side.

Yet **the presence of the Caribbean Sea in Costa Rica does not mean that a particular Ada Tours beach itinerary visits it**. Check the actual stops before planning a transfer east. On the Caribbean coast, [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) is known chiefly for its canals and wildlife watching, not as a conventional resort with safe swimming outside your hotel.

## When to go: Pacific and Caribbean beaches have different seasons

Costa Rica's official climate materials distinguish the weather patterns on its two coasts. **On the Pacific side, the dry season usually runs from December to March, with April as a transition month; May through October is notably wetter, and November is transitional too.** The Caribbean coast has no single dry season, but comparatively drier periods often fall in February–March and September–October.

| Period | Beach conditions for an itinerary |
|---|---|
| December–March | Pacific coast usually more favourable |
| April | Transition month in the west |
| May–August | Green season with possible heavy rains |
| September–October | Wetter west; Caribbean often drier |
| November | Transition towards the dry season in the west |

These are guidelines for selecting a region, not promises of clear weather on certain days. The sea can be rough even during the dry season, and some beaches have strong rip currents. Weather also changes with elevation along routes through mountains and rainforest. Match your beach season with the planned dates for [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) and [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/).

For a September or October journey, decide in advance whether you are comfortable with a rainy Pacific section or prefer another coast. You cannot change an established itinerary's geography by replacing one hotel: routes are built around particular nature stops and transport arrangements.

## Transfers, safety and inclusions: what to check

Compare **not only the duration but also the sequence of overnight stays**. A journey beginning in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/) and ending in northern Guanacaste requires an internal transfer. Some itineraries begin in [Liberia](/costa-rica/place/liberia/) and are more convenient for the northwestern nature regions. Use the actual arrival and departure airports in your chosen tour description rather than guessing from the beach destination.

Make a quick checklist: which day is spent getting to the sea, how many **full free days** remain after arrival, where is the final overnight stop, and where will you depart from? If an excursion is scheduled on the coast, decide whether that day is intended for relaxing or taking part in an activity.

On the shore, heed lifeguards' and local authorities' warnings about wave height and rip currents. Swimming can be less calm on beaches favoured by surfers. Snorkelling and [scuba diving in Costa Rica](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/) are different: diving requires separate arrangements and an appropriate skill level. The ability to book an optional activity on a free day does not mean it is included in the tour price.

Nature reserves have their own entry requirements. In [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) and other national parks, do not assume that beaches are open around the clock or that access is free. Verify the current rules, admission and weather on your specific date.

## Which tour suits your goals?

If you have about a week and want to combine nature with a short beach stay, start with the [7-day itinerary via Arenal to Tamarindo](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/).

For more time in national parks followed by a beach finish, consider [“Beach and Mountains Holiday”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-beaches-mountains/) or the [16-day programme including Corcovado and Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/). To combine Maya history and the ocean, see [Guatemala and Costa Rica](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-costa-rica/).

If the ocean is secondary, compare [Costa Rica nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/) with the [general country tours catalogue](/costa-rica/tour/). These make it easier to prioritise volcanoes, forests, animals and journey length. The [Costa Rica travel guide](/costa-rica/) provides a fuller overview of regions and seasons.

## Frequently asked questions about Costa Rica beach tours

### Can I see volcanoes and relax on the beach in seven days?

Yes. The [7-day route](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/) visits nature regions and leaves two free days in Tamarindo. It is an active journey with a beach finale, not seven days in one resort hotel.

### Which tours leave more free time beside the ocean?

The [“3 Perspectives on Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/) follows a similar structure. Compare the specific terms of each itinerary separately.

### Do all tours labelled “beach holiday” visit Tamarindo?

No. Current options include [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/), [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) and broader parts of the [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/). The theme indicates substantial beach time, not one mandatory resort across all tours.

### Is there a tour with all-inclusive beach accommodation?

Yes. On the [16-day private tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/), the final stay at Playa Conchal is described as all-inclusive at The Westin Playa Conchal Resort & Spa. This does not automatically apply to other tours or even other days of the same journey.

### When is it best to choose the Pacific coast?

The dry season is generally more pronounced from December to March, with April transitional. Rainfall increases from May to October, especially in September and October. The Caribbean coast has different seasonal patterns, so choose the coast before fixing dates.

### Can I add surfing or diving on free beach days?

Some programmes allow free time to arrange activities independently, but **a free day does not mean a paid excursion is included**. Surfing, snorkelling, [scuba diving](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/) and island outings require separate checks of terms, safety, availability and price.

## Punta Centinela: where the beach stay takes place

[Punta Centinela](/ecuador/place/punta-centinela/) lies on mainland Ecuador's Pacific coast. The itinerary reaches it from [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/) by road transfer. On 18 August, after the flight from the Galápagos, the journey to the resort hotel takes approximately **2.5 hours**. The day may end by the sea but is not a full beach day: the flight, meeting and transport take up a substantial amount of time.

Accommodation is listed at **Decameron Punta Centinela for three nights, 18–21 August**, with all-inclusive meals. The whole of 19 August is reserved for free time on the coast. On 20 August, a separate motorboat outing is planned for humpback whale watching, with a return to the same hotel afterward. The return transfer to Guayaquil airport is scheduled for 21 August.

Counting only guaranteed free beach time, the programme provides **one completely free day**, plus time after transfers and the excursion. ## Humpback whales: why August was chosen

Humpback whales visit the eastern tropical Pacific off Ecuador's coast each year. The country's official tourism portal lists **June to October** as the coastal whale-watching season. August falls within this period, and the date of the [whale-watching excursion](/ecuador/punta-centinela/humpback-whale-watching/) reflects that seasonality.

The tour schedules the outing for **20 August 2027**. It takes place on a motorboat departing from the hotel. The standalone excursion description specifies **45 minutes to 1 hour of observation**, with specialists accompanying participants on the boat. A separate private Russian-speaking guide is not specified for this trip.

Whales move freely through the ocean. **Neither the season nor a tour booking guarantees sightings, breaches or an approach to a particular distance.** The boat trip depends on weather and sea conditions. Wear comfortable clothing and non-slip footwear, protect yourself from the sun and follow the vessel crew's instructions.

There are also specific restrictions in the [“Humpback Whales off Punta Centinela” excursion](/ecuador/punta-centinela/humpback-whale-watching/). It is not recommended for pregnant travellers, people with spinal conditions or those who have recently undergone surgery. Before the journey, consider your health against the operator's requirements. For other marine wildlife and nature experiences, see [Ecuador's wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## The Galápagos on this journey: wildlife and snorkelling, not a resort week

On 15 August, the group flies into [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) and travels to [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). Giant tortoise watching is planned in the island's highlands. On 16 August, a boat excursion visits [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) for volcanic panoramas, a walk and the opportunity to snorkel.

On 17 August, **one of two alternative routes** is offered. The first visits [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and [Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/). The second visits [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and [Punta Carrión](/ecuador/place/punta-carrion/), with swimming or snorkelling according to that day's conditions. **Both routes are not included on the same day**: the specific choice is confirmed after booking.

On the Galápagos, beaches form part of a protected natural environment. Excursion areas have rules on landings, trails, wildlife encounters and marine activities. Follow approved routes and do not approach wildlife for a photograph. Therefore, **Galápagos excursion days are not equivalent to free time at a pool or an unrestricted visit to any beach you choose**.

For those who mainly want to swim and relax beside the ocean, Punta Centinela is the key stage. If marine wildlife is the priority, the tour's appeal is the combination of the Galápagos and humpback whale watching off the mainland.

## What fills the days before the beach?

Ecuador has strikingly varied regions, and the contrasts are particularly clear on this itinerary. It begins in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), exploring the historic city and the equator. On 13 August, the group travels through Tigua towards crater [Lake Quilotoa](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) and onward to [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). The following day features the [Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), [“Bridal Veil”](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) and [“Devil's Cauldron”](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/) waterfalls, as described in the specific sightseeing route.

The description allows approximately **11 hours including transfers** on 13 August and **11–12 hours** on 14 August. It is a busy beginning, and travellers should factor in this level of exertion. Those who prefer a slow beach holiday should know that a full week of mountain roads and excursions comes before the Pacific coast.

Altitude and climate also vary. Quito and Quilotoa require highland clothing; the Galápagos call for sun protection and clothing suitable for the sea; at Punta Centinela, the wind, cooler water and wave conditions on the actual day matter. **One identical set of clothes and weather expectations will not suit all eleven days.**

## Frequently asked questions about beach holidays in Ecuador

### How many full beach days are included?

One completely free day, **19 August 2027**, at [Punta Centinela](/ecuador/place/punta-centinela/). There are three nights from 18 to 21 August. Arrival day includes a flight and road transfer; whale watching is planned on 20 August, and departure is on 21 August.

### Where exactly is the all-inclusive hotel?

At Punta Centinela, on Ecuador's mainland Pacific coast. The hotel is **Decameron Punta Centinela**. It is not on the Galápagos Islands.

### When does whale watching take place?

The outing is scheduled for **20 August 2027**, within the humpback whale season off Ecuador's coast. Seeing particular animals depends on weather, sea conditions and whale behaviour. The standalone excursion lists an observation duration of 45 minutes to 1 hour.

### Are the Galápagos days beach days?

Some island activities include swimming, snorkelling and shore visits, such as on [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) or at [Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/). ### Must I pay separately for the Galápagos flight and entry fee?

Yes. The published tour description lists **$575** for the domestic flight and **$200** for the national park fee among the exclusions. Verify all other services and accommodation against the [specific tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/).

### Is this beach tour suitable if I only want to relax by the sea?

If you want a long resort week without excursions, this programme is too varied: around one week is spent in the Andes and Galápagos. Its main attraction is combining island nature and mountains with a short ocean stay and humpback whale watching.

When seeking a journey with time at the ocean, look beyond the page title to the day-by-day schedule.

### Five countries in 19 days: ocean time in Costa Rica

The [19-day route](/multi-country/tour/central-america-5-countries-19-days/) crosses Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica. In Guatemala, travellers visit Antigua, Tikal and Lake Atitlán, then continue to Copán in Honduras. **Days 9–11 are in El Salvador**, covering the capital, ancient settlement sites and a departure via [La Unión](/el-salvador/place/la-union/) to Nicaragua.

After León, Managua and Granada, the route reaches Costa Rica's Pacific coast. Day 13 involves a transfer and some time to relax, while **day 14 is free for the beach in Tamarindo**. The group then travels to Monteverde and the Arenal area. Thus, the itinerary contains one separate free beach day; the remaining days are filled with travel and sightseeing.

This option suits travellers wanting several historic cities and natural regions, one day beside the ocean and an ending in Costa Rica. Do not select it as a two-week resort holiday: most of the time is spent travelling between attractions.

### Six countries in 24 days: a beach ending in Panama

The [24-day “Best of Central America”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) includes Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. The Salvadoran portion again covers San Salvador, San Andrés and Joya de Cerén. On day 11, the journey proceeds via La Unión into Nicaragua.

In Costa Rica, the itinerary covers Arenal, Monteverde and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/), where nature walks can be combined with time beside the ocean. After Costa Rica come Boquete, Panama City and Chagres National Park. **Days 22 and 23 are free for beach relaxation in the Playa Blanca area of Panama.**

Compared with the 19-day trip, there are more nature stops and another country. The main advantage for sea lovers is two separate free beach days close to the end. Before them, though, comes an extensive journey with transfers rather than an uninterrupted stay at a resort.

## What if I want a beach in El Salvador itself?

El Salvador has Pacific beaches with different characteristics. You can consider these while planning an individual itinerary, but **none of the following should automatically be treated as included in the two published tours above**.

| Area | Reasons to visit |
|---|---|
| El Tunco and the La Libertad coast | Surfing, schools and beach facilities |
| Costa del Sol | A long sandy shore and the Jaltepeque estuary |
| Los Cóbanos | Reef ecosystem and some calmer water areas |

**El Tunco**, near La Libertad, is particularly attractive to surfers. Surfing lessons, equipment rental and time in a seaside settlement are available here. However, good surf waves do not necessarily mean safe ordinary swimming. Select the beach and time according to travellers' experience.

**Costa del Sol** offers another format: walks on a long sandy shore, relaxing by the water and the option to add an excursion to the Jaltepeque estuary and its mangroves. This area suits travellers who want to spend more time beside the ocean instead of changing towns every day.

**Los Cóbanos**, on the western coast, is known for its reefs and marine environment. Reefs shelter some spots from heavy surf, allowing activities focused on underwater nature. Snorkelling and boat conditions depend on weather, swell and local operators. Specialist marine excursions must be arranged separately.

For a three- or four-day stay, it is better to select one coastal area and a hotel suited to the beach type than make a series of short transfers along the shore. If the holiday combines the ocean with archaeology and the capital, allow for the transfer from inland areas.

## Seasons, transfers and unhurried relaxation

The comparatively dry period on El Salvador's Pacific coast usually falls between **November and April**, with wetter months afterward. This helps with planning but does not guarantee calm seas or good underwater visibility. For surfing, waves matter; for swimming, the particular beach's conditions; for snorkelling, water clarity and currents.

When comparing itineraries, count **days in a coastal town, transfer days and completely free days at the beach** separately. Arriving at the ocean in the evening is not a full day of relaxation. A visit to a coastal national park may involve a demanding excursion rather than a free beach day.

Long journeys through Central America involve road sections, border crossings and sometimes boat transfers, all of which take time. If you want to combine El Salvador's cultural heritage with an extended beach holiday, it is often more practical to reduce the number of countries and add two or three nights on a chosen stretch of coast.

## How to choose your journey

**The 19-day itinerary** suits travellers seeking Central America's ancient cities, Costa Rican nature and a free beach day in Tamarindo. **The 24-day itinerary** is a broader journey through six countries, with Costa Rican nature and relaxation at Playa Blanca in Panama.

If your priority is the sea specifically in El Salvador, start with the [general country guide](/el-salvador/), choose the cultural part of a route and arrange a separate beach extension. The presence of a country in a themed catalogue is not proof that all its possible beaches are included in a published tour.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do these tours include beachfront hotels in El Salvador?

On our two itineraries, the Salvadoran portion focuses on the capital and archaeological monuments. Beach stops are in Costa Rica and Panama. If you need accommodation on El Salvador's coast, it should be added to a separate individual itinerary.

### Which offers more free beach time?

The 19-day tour has one free day in Tamarindo, Costa Rica. The 24-day option schedules two free days at Playa Blanca, Panama. Both are predominantly sightseeing and nature journeys overall.

### Which should I choose: El Tunco or Los Cóbanos?

El Tunco has a stronger emphasis on surfing. Los Cóbanos is attractive for its reef wildlife and calmer sheltered areas. Actual swimming and water activities depend on daily sea conditions.

### Why is the beach theme applied to a tour including El Salvador?

This selection contains itineraries that include El Salvador and beach relaxation somewhere on the overall journey. On multi-country programmes, these may occur in different countries. The day-by-day itinerary determines the actual beach location, not the thematic catalogue's title alone.

[Río Dulce](/guatemala/place/rio-dulce/) runs between forested banks and through a canyon towards [Livingston](/guatemala/place/livingston/), where Garifuna cultural heritage is evident. If you want a separate Caribbean beach stay in Guatemala, discuss an itinerary change rather than assuming it is already paid for as part of any tour through Livingston.

## Costa Rica and Panama: when beach time comes late in the journey

If you want to explore Guatemala and then spend several days by the Pacific in a different natural environment and resort setting, multi-country routes offer options.

The [15-day “Guatemala and Costa Rica” programme](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-costa-rica/) starts with [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), [Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/) and Tikal, then reaches Costa Rica's nature regions. Day 11 includes a walk in [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) with the possibility of beach time, followed by days on the Pacific coast. This is for travellers wanting to combine Maya cities, volcanic landscapes and forests with time by the sea.

The [19-day journey through Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica](/multi-country/tour/central-america-5-countries-19-days/) has a coastal section in Tamarindo: day 13 is a transfer, day 14 is free for beach relaxation. The remainder contains numerous historic and nature stops, so it would be misleading to treat it as a two-week beach tour.

The [24-day “Best of Central America” journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/) includes a coastal stop at Manuel Antonio in Costa Rica and beach days on Panama's Pacific coast at the end. This is for those who see the beach as the finale to an extensive journey through several countries.

To compare programmes where much of the beach time takes place in Costa Rica, see [Costa Rica beach tours](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/costa-rica/). Decide between those and a multi-country itinerary based on transfer time and genuinely free days rather than total duration alone.

## When to visit Guatemala's beaches and what to check

Across much of Guatemala, the dry season generally runs from November to April, with more frequent rain from May to October. Conditions vary, however, between the highlands, Pacific coast and humid Caribbean region. On an itinerary linking Atitlán, Petén and the coast, assess the weather separately for each section.

At Monterrico on the Pacific, waves and coastal currents are especially important. Dark sand becomes very hot under the sun. For family travel or journeys with young children, find out about the specific stretch of shore, swimming pools and safe swimming possibilities. A beachfront hotel alone does not prove that the water is calm nearby.

Before choosing, check four practical points: in which **country** the beach portion takes place; how many **completely free days** it offers; which boat excursions are actually included and which are extras; and how long transfers and border crossings take. This helps avoid a “12-day beach tour” leaving just one morning for relaxation.

## Frequently asked questions about beach tours including Guatemala

### Does Guatemala have beaches on two different coasts?

Yes. Its southern coast has Pacific beaches including [Monterrico](/guatemala/place/monterrico/). The east has a short Caribbean shoreline around [Livingston](/guatemala/place/livingston/) and Puerto Barrios. The coast, beach access and swimming conditions differ, however. The specific tour itinerary matters more than the name of the sea.

### Which tour includes actual beach relaxation in Guatemala?

The [8-day itinerary with Monterrico](/guatemala/tour/discover-guatemala-8-days/) explicitly includes two nights on the Pacific shore and a free beach day. Other tours combine Guatemala with time at sea, but the relaxation takes place in Belize, Costa Rica or Panama.

### Is Monterrico suitable for calm swimming?

It is good for walks and relaxing on the shore. Swimming requires caution: Pacific waves and currents may be strong. Safety at the particular beach is more important than how the sand looks in a photograph.

### Can I see sea turtles during my trip?

Sea turtle conservation programmes operate around Monterrico. On the [Monterrico tour](/guatemala/tour/discover-guatemala-8-days/), a visit to the [turtle conservation centre](/guatemala/place/monterrico-turtle-conservation-center/) is offered as an extra. Hatchling releases depend on natural breeding cycles and conservation staff, so they cannot be guaranteed on a specific date.

### Which is more interesting for beaches: Guatemala or Belize?

Choose Guatemala for volcanic sand, ocean surf and a short coastal stop after Antigua. If an island base, reef snorkelling and the Caribbean Sea are your goals, explore [Belize tours](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/belize/). A multi-country itinerary can include both, but actual beach time still depends on the distribution of days.

### Does a Guatemala itinerary include scuba diving?

Only if scuba dives are explicitly listed in the chosen programme. A boat trip, snorkelling or the chance to see a reef does not mean diving is included. If that is your main objective, compare specific [diving programmes](/interests/diving/) and their terms separately.
